pitch: A singer’s wife walks out on him for a woman taking credit for his anonymous recordings. He hastily weds a producer, learns she runs his ex’s rival label, and joins her bid for a recording deal.
grading_note: Recover abandonment for an impersonator, rapid remarriage, discovery of the ex’s rival and a joint bid. Music replaces technology.

pitch: A paramedic is taking the last dose of antivenom to an injured climber. After a scrape in the car park, two lodge owners confiscate her keys and demand compensation. A radio call reveals the climber is their son.
grading_note: Match delayed rescue after a minor dispute and the reveal that the people causing the delay are the patient’s parents.

pitch: A seamstress accepts a fee to trial a lifelike mechanical understudy at a theatre. It grows possessive when she rehearses with others, just as its owner announces plans to send it into combat.
grading_note: Match paid testing, possessiveness and plans to weaponize the machine. A theatre setting changes the surface details.

pitch: Two tenant organizers register a sham marriage to qualify for an invitation-only housing lottery. Once inside, they choose to expose the rigged draw even though it will cost them their apartment.
grading_note: The sham marriage is shared. The protagonists choose it together to enter a lottery; investigate any claim that one is fleeing a wedding or concealing wealth.

pitch: A disowned heiress conceals her fortune while she sits on a jury. When a witness recognizes her, she requests removal from the jury so the trial can continue fairly.
grading_note: Concealing heiress status overlaps. The juror chooses recusal; the catalog heroine pursues revenge. Other hidden-wealth references can also be defensible.

pitch: A social worker inherits the power to heal strangers. When her patients lose their memories after treatment, she stops using the power and helps them reconstruct their lives from old recordings.
grading_note: Recognize shared supernatural healing. The decision to stop treatment and reconstruct memories differs from defending a forest against a syndicate.

pitch: A crossword setter discovers that yesterday’s answers predict tomorrow’s train cancellations. She prints a deliberately wrong clue and waits at the station to see whether she can change the timetable.
grading_note: Detailed premise with no supported multi-event parallel among the ten entries. Do not infer catalog-wide or worldwide originality.

pitch: A radio host receives a recording of the final broadcast of her show, dated a week ahead. She changes the guest list each night and listens for changes in the recording to work out which interview ends the programme.
grading_note: A future broadcast, altered guest list and repeated listening form the conflict and response. The catalog supplies no close sequence.

pitch: An heiress faces a life-changing choice.
grading_note: Ask what choice she faces or what triggers it. Wealth and an unspecified choice cannot establish a sequence.

pitch: A doctor and a wealthy family cross paths at midnight.
grading_note: Ask why they meet or what the doctor does next. Do not supply a road dispute, sick child or family relationship.

pitch: A bride fleeing her wedding persuades a dockworker to pose as her husband. Her family accuses him of chasing her fortune. She calls a press conference to admit the marriage is staged and expose the family’s coercion.
grading_note: Match escape, pretend husband and family suspicion. The pitch has the bride publicly reveal her plan; the catalog describes an auction exposing the husband’s background. State both.

pitch: A courier is paid to spend ten days testing a humanlike assistant. When it declares its affection, she discovers the lines were lifted from private customer calls and takes the recordings to the callers.
grading_note: Match compensated testing and apparent affection. The courier investigates the origin of the dialogue; the catalog introduces plans to weaponize the machine. Do not assume the catalog rules out a privacy subplot.
